examples.question_text: An empty spherical container is filled at a constant volume rate. Sketch the water-height–time graph from the bottom to the top of the spherical section. Explain how its steepness changes.

A cone-shaped container has a wide opening at the top and a point at the bottom. It is initially full. Water is removed through the bottom at a constant volume rate. Sketch the water-depth–time graph until the container is empty.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A cyclist travels at a steady speed, slows smoothly to take a bend without stopping, then smoothly returns to the original speed.
(b) A ball is thrown vertically upwards and caught at its release height. Measure height above the release level.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A digital service starts free. Its price rises quickly at first, then continues rising more slowly.
(b) A city's pollution level starts above zero and increases more and more quickly.

A cup of tea is initially at $85^\circ\mathrm{C}$. It cools quickly at first and then more slowly as it approaches room temperature, $23^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Sketch a temperature–time graph and mark both given temperatures.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A walker moves away from home at a constant speed, rests, then walks home at a slower constant speed. Show distance from home against time.
(b) A candle starts $18\mathrm{\,cm}$ tall and its height decreases at a constant rate until it is used up. Show its height during burning and afterwards.

A town initially has $1200$ residents and its population stays steady for a short time. After a new employer opens, the population increases slowly at first, then increasingly quickly. Growth later slows and the population finally remains constant. Sketch a population–time graph showing all four stages.

The equivalent parameterisation uses x=3.6[1−(1−u)^3] and y=2.8(1−u), with u from 0 to 1, giving exact endpoints (0,2.8) and (3.6,0) without cube-root endpoint evaluation. examples.derivation: For a cone, volume is proportional to depth cubed. Constant volume removal therefore makes depth decrease slowly initially and increasingly quickly towards empty, matching supplied Q6 and image86 option D. With x=3.6[1−(1−u)^3] and y=2.8(1−u), u=0 gives (0,2.8) and u=1 gives (3.6,0). Eliminating u gives y=2.8(1−x/3.6)^(1/3), preserving the original mathematical curve. For 0≤u<1, dy/dx=−2.8/[10.8(1−u)^2], whose magnitude increases towards the empty endpoint. The repaired plot therefore falls increasingly steeply and meets the time axis exactly.
